standard_prerequisites.name: Associated primes and their supports
standard_prerequisites.use: Relates an embedded associated prime to a strictly smaller associated prime whose support contributes to the dimension.

standard_prerequisites.name: Minimal primes of the support are associated
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the end of the counted proof (lines 44146-44148)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces an associated prime inside a given one, which yields an embedded prime when the local depth condition fails.

core_obligations: If p is an embedded associated prime, use the associated prime strictly below it to show that the support of the localised module at p has dimension at least one (proof lines 44125-44130).

Conversely, if the localised module at p has dimension at least one, use that minimal primes of the support are associated to find an associated prime inside p, so that p is embedded (proof lines 44130-44148).
proof_roadmap: Turn an embedded prime into a support of positive dimension (proof lines 44124-44130).
Turn positive-dimensional support into an embedded prime (proof lines 44130-44149).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a finite module over a Noetherian ring has no embedded associated prime exactly when it satisfies Serre's condition S one (statement lines 44113-44122). The proof does not invoke a general Cohen-Macaulay criterion: it shows that an embedded associated prime forces the localised support to have dimension at least one, and conversely that positive-dimensional localised support produces an associated prime strictly inside the given one by the correspondence between minimal primes of the support and associated primes (proof lines 44124-44149). Identifying the dimension of the localised support as the precise obstruction is the content. H2.
